However, serving these models in production environments presents unique challenges distinct from traditional machine learning inference. Unlike classification models that process fixed-size inputs and produce fixed-size outputs, LLMs are autoregressive generators. They produce text token-by-token, where each new token depends on the entire history of previously generated tokens. This sequential dependency creates a fundamental bottleneck in throughput and latency.

To address these challenges, modern inference servers (such as vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, and Hugging Face TGI) have developed sophisticated optimization techniques. This is computationally intensive but highly parallelizable, making it efficient on GPUs. During the **decode phase**, the model generates one token at a time. For each new token, the model must attend to all previous tokens (the prompt plus all previously generated tokens).
